title: Instinct Valued at $10 Billion: Can Personal Agent Justify Such a Price?
excerpt: Instinct aims to become a new layer of infrastructure between users and merchants, and transaction data shows that people are willing to let Personal Agents handle tasks on their behalf. However, transaction volume does not equal revenue; based on an entry value of 10 billion dollars, it would take roughly 300 times that amount in transactions to achieve a profit when exiting. This article analyzes the monetization strategies, the competition over distribution channels, and the main risks, concluding that it is worth studying but not worth investing in at the current price.
body:
*This article is a revised version of the investment memo submitted when I applied for an internship at IOSG Ventures. The data is current as of November 1, 2026, and all information comes from public sources; no internal company data was used.*

**My judgment is that Instinct aims to become a new layer of infrastructure between users and merchants, replacing the distribution roles previously held by search engines, app stores, and e-commerce platforms; current transaction data shows that this approach is logically feasible, but a valuation of $10 billion almost entirely consumes all the most optimistic growth prospects for the future.**

## Summary of Investment Views

Instinct is a Personal Agent designed for users. Users can assign tasks to it via text message or phone call, and it will handle things such as booking flights, making purchases, and dealing with everyday chores. Its founder, Noah Shinn, previously worked on research at Sierra. In August 2026, the company was reported to have completed a $250 million Series B funding round at a valuation of $2.5 billion; a month later, it announced a $1 billion Series C funding round at a valuation of $10 billion.[1](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/instinct-raises-1-billion-series-120300548.html)[2](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/26/viral-ai-startup-instinct-has-raised-350-million-at-a-2-5-billion-valuation/)

A four-fold surge in valuation within a month merely indicates fierce competition in the market for allocation, and it does not mean that $10 billion is a reasonable entry price. While writing this investment analysis, I kept doing some calculations: at this price point, how large does Instinct need to grow in order to achieve the return multiples required by venture capital funds?

Agents can now browse websites, use connected accounts, and place orders directly, having moved beyond the stage of merely answering questions. In September, Meta released Muse, and OpenAI released Dots; all of these companies are essentially doing the same thing. The entry of major platforms proves that this demand indeed exists, making it even harder for Instinct to maintain its position.[6](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/)[7](https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/)

The two figures provided by Instinct are worth noting. The annual transaction volume is close to $1 billion, with about half of those transactions related to travel, according to interviews with the founders. TechCrunch mentioned that the company has not disclosed the method used to calculate this annual figure. Among users who have access to sensitive data, around 80% remain loyal to the platform, again per the founders, though no specific time period was given. Those who are willing to share their email addresses and payment information are more likely to be loyal users, so this figure may be subject to selection bias. I consider these two figures as signals of demand, rather than evidence that a viable business model has already been established.[3](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/29/instinct-founder-said-more-than-50-of-transactions-on-the-platform-are-travel-related/)[4](https://barbellinsights.com/podcast/invest-like-the-best-with-patrick-oshaughnessy/noah-shinn-building-instinct-the-personal-agent-invest-like-the-best-ep-493?t=2083)

## Transaction volume is not yet revenue

In terms of commercialization, the founder’s vision is to offer a service “without subscription fees or ads, charging merchants only a transaction commission.” However, this remains just on paper—at present, according to third-party research firm Sacra, Instinct is completely free and generates no revenue at all; more importantly, neither its actual commission rate nor the cost of processing each task has been made public.[4](https://barbellinsights.com/podcast/invest-like-the-best-with-patrick-oshaughnessy/noah-shinn-building-instinct-the-personal-agent-invest-like-the-best-ep-493?t=2083)[5](https://sacra.com/c/instinct/)

The transaction amount represents money that passes through the platform; it is not Instinct’s revenue. I’ve prepared a sample calculation, and the last two figures are my assumptions, not actual company data.

These 10 million still do not take into account model invocation costs, payment fees, refunds, and customer service expenses. It may take multiple attempts and retries for an Agent to complete a booking, and sometimes human intervention is required. If merchants are unwilling to pay commissions, or if the operational costs exceed those commissions, no profit will be generated, no matter how fast usage increases.

To assess this business, one must at least look at the figures for each step: from the tasks initiated, to those actually completed, to the transaction amount after cancellations are deducted, to the actual amount paid by the merchant, and then to the profit per task after deducting execution costs — all of which should be broken down by travel, shopping, and services.

## Become a new layer between users and merchants

This is where the real bet of this funding round lies. Over the past decade, when users wanted to book flights or make purchases, they usually had to go through search engines, app stores, or e-commerce platforms — these entry points determined where traffic would flow and where the money would come from. Instinct’s assumption is that when users ask an Agent to “book a ticket to London next week” directly, the entry point shifts from the platform page to the Agent. **Those who earn users’ trust and can complete tasks reliably are closer to the distribution process.** The PDF states that a trusted Agent can become an important link between consumers and merchants, with potential advantages lying in trust, repeated use, and task execution quality, rather than having a more powerful model itself.[10](https://sequoiacap.com/companies/instinct)

This slot has not been taken yet; both sides are competing for it.

On one side are the large platforms that already have control over traffic. Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots also possess memory and cloud execution capabilities, but there is no publicly available comparable data showing that Instinct has better completion rates, lower costs, or higher user retention.[6](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/)[7](https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/) On the other side are the merchants who control products and orders. In September 2026, Amazon restricted Muse’s ability to process purchases on Amazon.com, claiming that the unauthorized Agent violated the terms of service and demanding that Meta remove Amazon from the system. An Axios report clearly identified the core issue: when an Agent places orders on behalf of a user, who owns the relationship with the user, and who is merely responsible for fulfillment?[11](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-blocks-metas-muse-ai-assistant-in-new-standoff-over-agentic-shopping/)[12](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/21/amazon-meta-muse-ai-agentic-shopping)

Some merchants also choose to cooperate. Sierra, together with Meta, is driving the development of the Personal Agent Protocol, with participants including Instinct, Shopify, Stripe, Walmart, and others. The goal is to establish guidelines for how Personal Agents can interact with merchants’ websites, APIs, or the merchants’ own Agents. It is an open standard, and once integrated, it remains accessible to multiple Agents; it does not constitute a barrier that is exclusive to Instinct.[13](https://sierra.ai/blog/introducing-personal-agent-protocol)

So the “new layer” is currently just a hypothesis. For it to become a reality, Instinct must accomplish at least three things simultaneously: users need to repeatedly assign tasks to it, merchants need to be willing to pay for completed transactions, and this position cannot be overtaken within a few quarters by Muse, Dots, or the merchants’ own interfaces. Completing a reservation does not mean that the merchant will pay Instinct.

## A good product can also have a poor entry price

I developed a reverse calculation model. Assuming the post-investment valuation is 10 billion, and the investment is held for 7 years, during which time it is diluted by 20% due to subsequent financing; priority liquidation rights, management fees, and taxes are not taken into account. These are all assumptions in the modeling, not actual terms.

```text
Exit valuation = Entry valuation × Target return multiple ÷ (1 − Dilution ratio)
3x return: 10 billion × 3 ÷ 0.8 = 37.5 billion USD, with an IRR of approximately 17.0% over 7 years
5x return: 10 billion × 5 ÷ 0.8 = 62.5 billion USD, with an IRR of approximately 25.8% over 7 years
```

Venture capital typically requires that a single project have a potential return of more than 5 times its investment. Assuming an exit valuation of 10 times the revenue, $62.5 billion would correspond to an annual revenue of $6.25 billion. If a 2% commission could be charged on all transactions, this would require annual transaction volumes of $312.5 billion, which is over 300 times the current level of around $1 billion—assuming consistent calculations on both sides. If only a portion of transactions generate revenue, the requirements would be even higher.

If 10 billion is actually the pre-investment valuation, and after raising another 1 billion, the post-investment value is around 11 billion, then the threshold rises even further. The conclusion is straightforward: having a good product and making a sound investment decision are two separate matters that need to be evaluated independently.

## Three main risks

I believe there are three areas that are most likely to render this investment logic ineffective, with each corresponding to a signal that can be verified.

1. **The business model is not viable.** The commissions generated are not sufficient to cover the costs associated with the models, payments, and customer service. It is necessary to examine the merchant contracts, the actual commissions received, and the profit per completed task.  
2. **Platform competition.** Muse or Dots may match or even surpass Instinct in handling similar tasks, prompting users to switch at any time. Comparative tests should be conducted on tasks related to travel, shopping, and scheduling, and interviews should be held to understand why users stay or leave.  
3. **Trust issues.** Errors in permissions or unauthorized actions can lead to users leaving immediately. Media reports in August highlighted early users’ concerns regarding privacy and security. It is important to assess the error rate of sensitive operations, any incident records, and the results of security audits.\[8\]\[9\]

In the most pessimistic scenario, Instinct proves that people do need Personal Agents, but in the end it is the larger platforms that end up controlling user relationships and reaping the profits.

A transaction volume of $1 billion and an 80% retention rate are excellent results in terms of product performance reviews. They indicate that users are willing to entrust ticket booking and payment to an Agent. However, investors are looking for a value of $10 billion, and achieving that requires a transaction volume more than 300 times higher. Since the product is only half developed, this investment could still result in losses — both of these situations apply to this company.

b0251417ed6d038c8b36eb27b9b39d3bc72126dd.source: 这里才是这轮融资真正在赌的东西。过去十年，用户要订机票、买东西，通常要经过搜索引擎、应用商店或电商平台，这些入口决定了流量往哪里去、钱从哪里抽。Instinct 的假设是，当用户把“帮我订一张下周去伦敦的票”直接交给 Agent，入口就从平台页面移到了 Agent 这一侧。**谁被用户信任、谁能稳定把任务做完，谁就更靠近分发位置。** PDF 里的表述是，一个受信任的 Agent 可能成为消费者与商家之间重要的连接，潜在优势是信任、反复使用和执行质量，而不是模型本身更强。[10](https://sequoiacap.com/companies/instinct)
b0251417ed6d038c8b36eb27b9b39d3bc72126dd.context: 成为用户与商家之间的新一层
b0251417ed6d038c8b36eb27b9b39d3bc72126dd.translation: This is where the real bet of this funding round lies. Over the past decade, when users wanted to book flights or make purchases, they usually had to go through search engines, app stores, or e-commerce platforms — these entry points determined where traffic would flow and where the money would come from. Instinct’s assumption is that when users ask an Agent to “book a ticket to London next week” directly, the entry point shifts from the platform page to the Agent. **Those who earn users’ trust and can complete tasks reliably are closer to the distribution process.** The PDF states that a trusted Agent can become an important link between consumers and merchants, with potential advantages lying in trust, repeated use, and task execution quality, rather than having a more powerful model itself.[10](https://sequoiacap.com/companies/instinct)

7e51aa5a8b0798f52d0e579e270da1e2d957ae11.source: 这层位置现在还没有被拿走，两边都在抢。
7e51aa5a8b0798f52d0e579e270da1e2d957ae11.context: 成为用户与商家之间的新一层
7e51aa5a8b0798f52d0e579e270da1e2d957ae11.translation: This slot has not been taken yet; both sides are competing for it.

cc5b580b0dbe77fa7e868d092bd66f16ea4e479d.source: 一边是已经掌握流量的大平台。Meta 的 Muse 和 OpenAI 的 Dots 同样有记忆和云端执行能力，目前没有公开、可比的数据显示 Instinct 的完成率、成本或留存更好。[6](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/)[7](https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/) 另一边是掌握商品和订单的商家。2026 年 9 月，Amazon 切断了 Muse 在 Amazon.com 上的购物权限，公开说法是未经授权的 Agent 违反使用条款，并要求 Meta 把 Amazon 从体验里拿掉。Axios 的报道把核心问题说得很直，当 Agent 替用户下单时，谁拥有用户关系，谁只是在履约。[11](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-blocks-metas-muse-ai-assistant-in-new-standoff-over-agentic-shopping/)[12](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/21/amazon-meta-muse-ai-agentic-shopping)
cc5b580b0dbe77fa7e868d092bd66f16ea4e479d.context: 成为用户与商家之间的新一层
cc5b580b0dbe77fa7e868d092bd66f16ea4e479d.translation: On one side are the large platforms that already have control over traffic. Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots also possess memory and cloud execution capabilities, but there is no publicly available comparable data showing that Instinct has better completion rates, lower costs, or higher user retention.[6](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/)[7](https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/) On the other side are the merchants who control products and orders. In September 2026, Amazon restricted Muse’s ability to process purchases on Amazon.com, claiming that the unauthorized Agent violated the terms of service and demanding that Meta remove Amazon from the system. An Axios report clearly identified the core issue: when an Agent places orders on behalf of a user, who owns the relationship with the user, and who is merely responsible for fulfillment?[11](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-blocks-metas-muse-ai-assistant-in-new-standoff-over-agentic-shopping/)[12](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/21/amazon-meta-muse-ai-agentic-shopping)

ed7a7c945f7711d18f79a46fd7fc2bec80079629.source: 也有商家选择合作。Sierra 与 Meta 一起推动 Personal Agent Protocol，参与方包括 Instinct、Shopify、Stripe、Walmart 等，目标是约定 Personal Agent 如何与商家的网站、API 或商家自己的 Agent 交互。它是开放标准，接入之后同时对多家 Agent 开放，本身不会成为 Instinct 独占的壁垒。[13](https://sierra.ai/blog/introducing-personal-agent-protocol)
ed7a7c945f7711d18f79a46fd7fc2bec80079629.context: 成为用户与商家之间的新一层
ed7a7c945f7711d18f79a46fd7fc2bec80079629.translation: Some merchants also choose to cooperate. Sierra, together with Meta, is driving the development of the Personal Agent Protocol, with participants including Instinct, Shopify, Stripe, Walmart, and others. The goal is to establish guidelines for how Personal Agents can interact with merchants’ websites, APIs, or the merchants’ own Agents. It is an open standard, and once integrated, it remains accessible to multiple Agents; it does not constitute a barrier that is exclusive to Instinct.[13](https://sierra.ai/blog/introducing-personal-agent-protocol)

1b3adfe0b70e69d40befcb6512d2773813c942a7.source: 所以“新的一层”现在只是假设。要成立，Instinct 至少得同时做到三件事，用户反复把任务交给它，商户愿意为完成的交易付钱，而且这个位置不会在几个季度里被 Muse、Dots 或商家自己的入口抹平。完成一笔预订，并不等于商户会向 Instinct 付钱。
1b3adfe0b70e69d40befcb6512d2773813c942a7.context: 成为用户与商家之间的新一层
1b3adfe0b70e69d40befcb6512d2773813c942a7.translation: So the “new layer” is currently just a hypothesis. For it to become a reality, Instinct must accomplish at least three things simultaneously: users need to repeatedly assign tasks to it, merchants need to be willing to pay for completed transactions, and this position cannot be overtaken within a few quarters by Muse, Dots, or the merchants’ own interfaces. Completing a reservation does not mean that the merchant will pay Instinct.

0083301bd88c5f40be9ee69ff2ffd121e5ec4105.source: ## 好产品也可能是差的入场价
0083301bd88c5f40be9ee69ff2ffd121e5ec4105.translation: ## A good product can also have a poor entry price

87935a40ff7f9980394b85b40d703e6ffbc5b647.source: 我做了一个反推模型。假设 100 亿是投后估值，持有 7 年，期间因后续融资被稀释 20%，不考虑优先清算权、管理费和税。这些都是建模假设，不是实际条款。
87935a40ff7f9980394b85b40d703e6ffbc5b647.context: 好产品也可能是差的入场价
87935a40ff7f9980394b85b40d703e6ffbc5b647.translation: I developed a reverse calculation model. Assuming the post-investment valuation is 10 billion, and the investment is held for 7 years, during which time it is diluted by 20% due to subsequent financing; priority liquidation rights, management fees, and taxes are not taken into account. These are all assumptions in the modeling, not actual terms.

166c2fdd85fbb8662765df6a5ec58e345dea9f32.source:
退出估值 = 入场估值 × 目标回报倍数 ÷ (1 − 稀释比例)
3 倍回报：100 亿 × 3 ÷ 0.8 = 375 亿美元，7 年 IRR 约 17.0%
5 倍回报：100 亿 × 5 ÷ 0.8 = 625 亿美元，7 年 IRR 约 25.8%
166c2fdd85fbb8662765df6a5ec58e345dea9f32.context: 好产品也可能是差的入场价
166c2fdd85fbb8662765df6a5ec58e345dea9f32.translation:
Exit valuation = Entry valuation × Target return multiple ÷ (1 − Dilution ratio)
3x return: 10 billion × 3 ÷ 0.8 = 37.5 billion USD, with an IRR of approximately 17.0% over 7 years
5x return: 10 billion × 5 ÷ 0.8 = 62.5 billion USD, with an IRR of approximately 25.8% over 7 years

48558c8bc1b548485be5b4f692366c630805009c.source: 风险投资通常要求单个项目有 5 倍以上的潜力。再假设退出时按 10 倍收入估值，625 亿美元对应 62.5 亿美元年收入。如果所有交易都能按 2% 收佣金，就需要每年 3,125 亿美元交易额，是现在约 10 亿美元的 300 多倍，而且前提是两边口径一致。只有一部分交易能收钱的话，要求还会更高。
48558c8bc1b548485be5b4f692366c630805009c.context: 好产品也可能是差的入场价
48558c8bc1b548485be5b4f692366c630805009c.translation: Venture capital typically requires that a single project have a potential return of more than 5 times its investment. Assuming an exit valuation of 10 times the revenue, $62.5 billion would correspond to an annual revenue of $6.25 billion. If a 2% commission could be charged on all transactions, this would require annual transaction volumes of $312.5 billion, which is over 300 times the current level of around $1 billion—assuming consistent calculations on both sides. If only a portion of transactions generate revenue, the requirements would be even higher.

55719b45cf2eabf0fa7022075dcb01d34366c94d.source: 如果 100 亿其实是投前估值，加上 10 亿融资后投后约 110 亿，门槛还要再抬一点。这笔账的结论很直接，产品做得好和这笔投资划算是两件事，要分开判断。
55719b45cf2eabf0fa7022075dcb01d34366c94d.context: 好产品也可能是差的入场价
55719b45cf2eabf0fa7022075dcb01d34366c94d.translation: If 10 billion is actually the pre-investment valuation, and after raising another 1 billion, the post-investment value is around 11 billion, then the threshold rises even further. The conclusion is straightforward: having a good product and making a sound investment decision are two separate matters that need to be evaluated independently.

3352a16521ccb5ff3595b0c385ebd080860ed3d9.source: 我认为最可能让这个投资逻辑失效的有三处，每处都对应一个可以检验的信号。
3352a16521ccb5ff3595b0c385ebd080860ed3d9.translation: I believe there are three areas that are most likely to render this investment logic ineffective, with each corresponding to a signal that can be verified.

3164af1571c3706e563396a755a3663ce47b9d3c.source:
1. **单位经济不成立。** 佣金覆盖不了模型、支付和客服成本。要看商户合同、实收佣金和单个完成任务的利润。
2. **平台竞争。** Muse 或 Dots 在同类任务上追平甚至超过 Instinct，用户随时换走。要在同样的差旅、购物、日程任务上做对比测试，并访谈用户为什么留下或离开。
3. **信任出事。** 权限错误或未经授权的操作会直接赶走用户。8 月已有媒体报道早期用户对隐私和安全的担忧。要看敏感操作的出错率、事故记录和安全审查结果。\[8\]\[9\]
3164af1571c3706e563396a755a3663ce47b9d3c.translation:
1. **The business model is not viable.** The commissions generated are not sufficient to cover the costs associated with the models, payments, and customer service. It is necessary to examine the merchant contracts, the actual commissions received, and the profit per completed task.  
2. **Platform competition.** Muse or Dots may match or even surpass Instinct in handling similar tasks, prompting users to switch at any time. Comparative tests should be conducted on tasks related to travel, shopping, and scheduling, and interviews should be held to understand why users stay or leave.  
3. **Trust issues.** Errors in permissions or unauthorized actions can lead to users leaving immediately. Media reports in August highlighted early users’ concerns regarding privacy and security. It is important to assess the error rate of sensitive operations, any incident records, and the results of security audits.\[8\]\[9\]

31e9a6df4213d8edf89fefb46416795d8852058b.source: 最悲观的情形是，Instinct 证明了人们需要 Personal Agent，最后掌握用户关系、拿走利润的却是更大的平台。
31e9a6df4213d8edf89fefb46416795d8852058b.translation: In the most pessimistic scenario, Instinct proves that people do need Personal Agents, but in the end it is the larger platforms that end up controlling user relationships and reaping the profits.

2701132cb156307f504b49a0ff9f5d9a7cab7ab4.source: 10 亿美元的交易额、80% 的留存，放在产品复盘里都是好成绩。它们说明用户愿意把订票和付款交给一个 Agent。可投资人买的是 100 亿美元的价格，这个价格要靠 300 多倍的交易额才能兑现。产品已经成了一半，这笔投资还可能亏钱，两件事在这家公司身上同时成立。
2701132cb156307f504b49a0ff9f5d9a7cab7ab4.translation: A transaction volume of $1 billion and an 80% retention rate are excellent results in terms of product performance reviews. They indicate that users are willing to entrust ticket booking and payment to an Agent. However, investors are looking for a value of $10 billion, and achieving that requires a transaction volume more than 300 times higher. Since the product is only half developed, this investment could still result in losses — both of these situations apply to this company.
